He played [[college basketball]] for the [[College of Central Florida|College of Central Florida Patriots]] and the [[Texas A&M Aggies men's basketball|Texas A&M Aggies]]. ==High school career== Jackson attended [[Mira Costa High School]]. He missed a month and a half with a wrist injury as a senior.{{cite news |title=Jackson, Mira Costa hang on in tight boys basketball win at Peninsula |url=https://www.dailybreeze.com/2016/02/03/jackson-mira-costa-hang-on-in-tight-boys-basketball-win-at-peninsula/ |access-date=December 29, 2022 |work=[[Daily Breeze]] |date=February 3, 2016 |archive-date=December 29, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221229223235/https://www.dailybreeze.com/2016/02/03/jackson-mira-costa-hang-on-in-tight-boys-basketball-win-at-peninsula/ |url-status=live }} ==College career== Jackson began his college career at the [[College of Central Florida]]. As a sophomore, he averaged 18.3 points, 5.2 rebounds and three assists per game. Jackson transferred to [[Texas A&M Aggies men's basketball|Texas A&M]], choosing the Aggies over [[Arkansas Razorbacks men's basketball|Arkansas]], [[LSU Tigers men's basketball|LSU]], [[Texas Longhorns men's basketball|Texas]] and [[West Virginia Mountaineers men's basketball|West Virginia]].{{cite web |last=Evans |first=Corey |title=Texas A&M lands junior college standout Quenton Jackson |url=https://basketballrecruiting.rivals.com/news/texas-a-m-lands-junior-college-standout-quenton-jackson |website=[[Rivals.com]] |access-date=December 29, 2022 |date=April 13, 2019 |archive-date=December 29, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221229223232/https://basketballrecruiting.rivals.com/news/texas-a-m-lands-junior-college-standout-quenton-jackson |url-status=live }} He averaged 8.8 points and 2.9 rebounds per game as a junior.{{cite news |last=Zwerneman |first=Brent |title=Quenton Jackson finds his range in College Station |url=https://www.houstonchronicle.com/texas-sports-nation/college/article/Quenton-Jackson-finds-his-range-in-College-Station-15124398.php |access-date=December 29, 2022 |work=[[Houston Chronicle]] |date=March 11, 2020 |archive-date=December 29, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221229223234/https://www.houstonchronicle.com/texas-sports-nation/college/article/Quenton-Jackson-finds-his-range-in-College-Station-15124398.php |url-status=live }} As a senior, Jackson averaged 10.4 points, 2.4 rebounds and 1.7 assists per game. Following the season, he opted to return for an additional year of eligibility.{{cite web |last=Hattersley |first=Andrew |title=WATCH: Quenton Jackson confirms return to Texas A&M for another year. |url=https://247sports.com/college/texas-am/Article/Quenton-Jackson-Texas-AM-Basketball-Buzz-Williams-Aggies-Extra-Season--164117070/ |website=247 Sports |access-date=December 29, 2022 |date=May 15, }} ==Professional career== ===Washington Wizards / Capital City Go-Go (2022–2023)=== After going undrafted in the [[2022 NBA draft]], Jackson signed an [[Exhibit 10]] contract with the [[Washington Wizards]] on September 13, 2022.{{cite web|first=Luke|last=Adams|title=Wizards Officially Sign Quenton Jackson|url=https://www.hoopsrumors.com/2022/09/wizards-officially-sign-quenton-jackson.html|website=HoopsRumors.com|date=September 13, 2022|access-date=February 10, 2023|archive-date=September 27, 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220927160415/https://www.hoopsrumors.com/2022/09/wizards-officially-sign-quenton-jackson.html|url-status=live}} He was waived by the Wizards on October 15, and he subsequently joined the [[Capital City Go-Go]], the Wizards' [[NBA G League]] affiliate.{{cite web|title=Wizards announce 2022-23 opening night two-way contract with the Wizards.{{cite web|title=Wizards sign Quenton Jackson to two-way contract|url=https://www.nba.com/wizards/news/wizards-sign-quenton-jackson-to-two-way-contract|website=NBA.com|date=February 10, 2023|access-date=February 10, 2023|archive-date=February 10, web|first=Alex|last=Kirschenbaum|title=Quenton Jackson Released By Wizards|url=https://www.hoopsrumors.com/2023/07/quenton-jackson-released-by-wizards.html|website=HoopsRumors.com|date=July 24, September 8, 2023, Jackson signed with the [[Chicago Bulls]],{{cite tweet|author=Chicago Bulls|title=Roster Update: We have signed guards Quenton Jackson and Max Heidegger to Exhibit-10 contracts.|number=1700188552573661399|user=chicagobulls|date=September 8, 2023|access-date=September 8, 2023}} but was waived on October 16.{{cite tweet|author=Chicago Bulls|title=Transaction: We have waived guard Quenton Jackson.|number=1713925312994570310|user=chicagobulls|date=October 16, 2023|access-date=October 16, 2023}} On November 9, he joined the [[Windy City Bulls]].{{cite web|title=Windy City Bulls Announce 2023 Training Camp Roster|url=https://windycity.gleague.nba.com/news/the-windy-city-bulls-announce-2023-training-camp-roster|website=NBA.com|date=November 2, 2023|access-date=November 9, 2023}} ===Indiana Pacers / Mad Ants / Noblesville Boom (2024-present)=== On March 4, 2024, Jackson signed a [[two-way contract]] with the [[Indiana Pacers]].{{cite web|title=Indiana Pacers Sign Quenton Jackson to Two-Way Contract|url=https://www.nba.com/pacers/news/indiana-pacers-sign-quenton-jackson-to-two-way-contract|website=NBA.com|date=March 4, 2024|access-date=March 5, 2024}} On July 27, 2024, Jackson signed another two-way contract with the Pacers.{{cite web|title=Indiana Pacers Sign Jackson and Newton to Two-Way Contracts|url=https://www.nba.com/pacers/news/indiana-pacers-sign-jackson-and-newton-to-two-way-contracts|website=NBA.com|date=July 27, 2024|access-date=July 27, 2024}} Jackson made his first career start on November 21, against the [[2024–25 Houston Rockets season|Houston Rockets]], and scored a career–high 24 points on 10–of–12 shooting in the 130–113 loss.{{cite web | last=Holkko | first=Shaun | title=Texas A&M alumnus Quenton Jackson scores career-high in first NBA start for Indiana Pacers | website=Aggies Wire|publisher=USA Today | date=2024-11-22 | url=https://aggieswire.usatoday.com/story/sports/college/aggies/mens-basketball/2024/11/21/texas-aggies-basketball-indiana-pacers-quenton-jackson/76490622007/ | access-date=2025-11-04}} Jackson also had a standout performance against the [[2025–26 Golden State Warriors season|Golden State Warriors]] on November 1, 2025, in which the Pacers snapped their five game losing streak at the beginning of the season, carried by his 25-point, 10-assist performance.{{cite web | title=Pacers' Quenton Jackson: Erupts for double-double | website=CBS Sports | date=2025-11-02 | url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/pacers-quenton-jackson-erupts-for-double-double/ | access-date=2025-12-06}} This was a new career-high for Jackson.
